patterns: Common opening in 11 of 18 games (4 lost, 7 won): with fewer than 2 own towers within 500 and a knight within 250, the defence rule walks the queen 2-7 lines to a new tower site, always forward (depth +12 to +263); the knights (speed 100 vs her 60) catch her and block the last steps (moved < 20). One walk against one 4-knight group cost 1-11 HP in won races, the same as lost 917983421 (7), so the walk alone does not decide races; lost walks were longer and costlier (mean 5.75 lines/12.0 HP vs 3.7/5.0).

Loss per line follows the number of knights near her and whether she moves. Pooled in both groups a moving queen lost 0.34-0.36 HP per knight-turn within 250, a still one (moved < 20) 0.53-0.58; still with 5+ knights within 250 cost 4.1 per line. Lost races had 3.5x the still knight-turns of won races (113 vs 32) and 1.7x the moving ones (257 vs 153). Still lines carry 49 HP of the 82-HP batch gap (lossK20 totals 154 vs 72).

Top-ups are safe until a knight is one step away: BUILD on an own tower with the nearest knight >= 155 cost 0 HP in both groups (15 lost and 42 won lines); with a knight < 155 it cost 36 HP on 11 lines in 3 lost races (917846452, 917986438, 917982299) vs 4 HP on 2 lines in won races. Rule chain: play() runs defence -> kite -> touch (top-up < 700) -> flee (BUILD nearest own tower); beside her tower with knights on several sides kite() finds no heading that gains 5 (KITE_PULL=100, step must end under cover, the site blocks the escape), so she falls through to a BUILD and stands while all knights reach her.

The lost-race excess comes in bursts of 3+ knights touching: 65 HP on lines with -k >= 3 in lost races vs 9 in won ones (47 of the 65 in 917982299). Bursts happen while she stands at her tower or walks to a new site with 6 knights.

Second groups: in lost races the next enemy group reached her before the first was cleared (5+ knights within 500 on at least one window line in 6/9 lost vs 2/9 won); in won races it usually arrived after the clear (917982912, 917848273, 917984006) and cost 0-2 HP. Overlap without standing still stayed cheap (lost 917849541: 5 HP with 6 knights; won 917845973: -k1 per line with 4 knights).

Defence re-trigger: in 2 lost races (917847704 t26, 917982299 t35) a kiting step carried the queen past 500 of her second tower (one of only 164 HP), THREAT_TOWERS_NEAR fired again and sent her on a 5-6 line forward walk with 3-7 knights (12 and 18 HP, then 21 HP of top-ups in 917982299). Never seen in won races.

Lost races met the wave deeper and the knights were fresher: queen distance from her home side at contact mean 507 vs 309 (>= 400 in 8/9 lost vs 2/9 won), mean knight HP within 500 at contact 15.7 vs 11.3. Knight-turns within 250 doubled (mean 41 vs 21) while tower damage per threatened line was the same (5.6 vs 5.3).

More tower HP near her at contact did not protect: lost races had more own tower HP within 500 (mean 1086 vs 781; 2+ towers within 500 in 5/9 lost vs 2/9 won). Single-target fire of 3-8 per tower per turn cannot clear 6-7 knights of 15-20 HP before they wear down a still queen.

The first-wave cost was at least the final margin in 7 of 9 lost races (917983421 12 vs 12, 917847704 24 vs 2, 917987738 13 vs 12, 917846452 22 vs 9, 917986438 13 vs 13, 917849541 5 vs 4, 917982299 57 vs 14); 917848591 (8 vs 13) and 917986939 (0 vs 36) were lost elsewhere. In the other three the first wave was decisive, its loss exceeding the final margin: 917982303 8 vs 7, 917850072 12 vs 3, 917983316 19 vs 2.

Every HP lost to knights is one knight touching her (1 HP per knight per turn). Kiting does not shake a glued knight (near 50-55), because knights move 100 per turn and the queen 60. Glued kite turns cost about 1 HP per glued knight: 917850072 t30-37 (1 x8), 917846333 t31-34 (2,2,2,3), 917986603 t29-33 (2,2,2,1,1). Only tower kills end it.

The costliest turns are stands on an own tower with knights adjacent. When knights are on several sides, no kite heading gains 5, so the touch rule tops up the tower she touches, usually the one built at contact. Examples: 917983316 t37-39 (3,4,3) on tower 1 at 456-552 HP; 917846333 t29-30 (2,3) and t35-37 (3,4,4) on tower 23 at 180-448 HP; 917850072 t28-29 (2,2) on tower 20 at 184-280 HP. All three batch games with at least 12 HP lost in the window had a merged wave. A second enemy group joined 3-5 turns after contact (eK500 3-4 to 7, knight HP 57-70 to 104-125), while the queen was anchored at a tower built at or just before contact (917983316 L, 917850072 L, 917846333 W).

The knights stayed at 150-250 for 9-10 turns before the first hit (contact share 0.25 and 0.11) while the towers dealt 7-9 per turn. Standing at a tower then cost nothing because no knight was adjacent (917850563 at tower 11, 788-796 HP; 917849997 at tower 21).

The defence walk: in 7 of 18 games, contact catches the queen walking from her only tower to a free site (the defence rule: fewer than 2 own towers within 500). The knights glue to her during the walk or block it (moved 5-16), and she loses 1-3 HP per turn until the new tower stands: 917982303 t21-24 (1,1,2,2, the decisive loss), 917846920 t20-23 (1,1,1,2), 917986689 t21-23 (2,1,2), 917986603 t27-28 (2,3), 917845739 t22-23 (1,1). patterns: Most first-wave HP in lost races goes while the queen stands or is blocked. In my 8 lost races, 55 of 87 HP (63%) were lost on turns where she moved < 40; in my 10 won races it was 8 of 36 HP (22%). Per game: 6.9 vs 0.8 HP standing, and 4.0 vs 2.8 HP while moving 40 or more. 7 of 8 lost races vs 1 of 10 won races lost any HP standing. Across all 106 races (my parser): 5.75 vs 1.95 standing and 6.77 vs 3.92 moving. A standing contact turn costs 2.2 HP and a moving one 1.3, because knights reach a standing queen from about 155 but a fleeing one only from about 95.

In my lost races the standing turns are mostly not voluntary top-ups. They are BUILDs that had no effect (no new tower, no HP gain on the next line) while the queen moved < 40. 917851589: 8 turns, 17 HP; BUILD 17 left her 102-105 from the tower centre, just outside touch distance, apparently held there by the knights' collisions. 917850428: 20 turns, 20 HP; defence BUILD 19 slid along an obstacle at 1-12 per turn. No won race in my batch has such a turn.

The defence tower is built during contact in lost races. 6 of 8 lost vs 1 of 10 won races lost HP on defence-rule turns (fewer than 2 own towers within 500, knights within 250). Constructing with the nearest knight < 155 was always hit: 917846715 t23 (139), 917988302 t22 (48), 917985474 t23 (91), 917851589 t25 (69), 917984405 t34 (52). Constructing at 151 or more never was: 917847525 t20 (208), 917986876 t24 (151), 917984245 t35 (183). The rule fires only at knights within 250 (THREAT_RANGE), which is too late for a walk plus a construction. In 917988302 and 917984405 the defence site lay toward the knights.

Two own towers within 500 at contact: 1 of 8 lost vs 7 of 10 won in my batch, and those 7 won races lost 0-2 HP each. Tower count is not sufficient, though. Across all 106 races, the 17 lost races with 2 or more towers within 500 at contact still lost 13.8 HP each, against 2.5 in the 33 won ones. In that subgroup, HP lost to the kite-found-no-step fallback (top-up or BUILD on an existing tower with knights within 250) is 5.65 vs 0.61, and the waves are bigger (up to 5.9 vs 4.4 knights within 500; 57 vs 45 knight HP at contact). My batch's only such lost race (917988196) lost 0, so I could not inspect these races.

When knights are within 250, 2 towers are within 500, and kite() returns no step, the bot tops up the touched tower or walks with BUILD to its nearest tower. In 917851589 the nearest tower lay on the knights' side (toward the enemy corner), so the walk went into them and failed for 8 turns. In 917846826 (won) two standing top-ups took 3 and 4 hits. Suspected cause: with KITE_PULL=100 the score is nearest-knight distance minus nearest-tower distance, which cannot gain 5 when knights and tower lie in the same direction. This is inferred: the trace has no knight positions, and the tower centre was trilaterated in one game.

A second group joins during contact in 5 of 8 lost vs 2 of 10 won races in my batch (21/44 vs 16/62 across all races). Examples: 917985474 (4 spawned at contact, 6 within 500 at t26), 917851589 (6 at t27), 917849006 (6 at t30, another group at t38), 917850428 (13 of its 20 HP went to the group spawned at t27). Across all races, contact turns while moving show 4.0 knights and 46 HP within 500 in lost races vs 3.2 and 31 in won races, with the same tower damage (5.3 vs 5.1 per turn).

Contact lasts longer in lost races. The longest run of consecutive turns with knight damage is 6.9 in lost vs 1.6 in won races in my batch (6.4 vs 3.4 across all races). In won races a knight that reaches the queen dies within 1-3 turns (917847525, 917846967, 917986876, 917989288).

Single-tower kiting: KITE_PULL binds the orbit to the nearest tower. In 917849006 the queen circled tower 7 at 92-98 for 20 turns while the fresh tower 12 (range about 250) was 266-336 away, so cov stayed 1 and one knight was on her for 9 turns. The won kiting races (917846967, 917986354, 917847205, 917989288) kited under 2 towers and kept knights 90-155 or more away.

The 500-radius threshold makes the queen dither. In 917846826 (won only because she started with 100 HP), tower 19 sat at 461-550 from her and switched the defence rule on and off. Walks toward site 13 and kite MOVEs alternated for 13 turns, site 13 was never built in the window, and she lost 26 HP. This does not separate lost from won in my batch, but it is a clear HP sink.

patterns: Both first-wave disasters in the batch (917851391: 58 HP, 917986038: 29 HP; final deficits 40 and 26) took most of their loss while the queen STOOD (moved < 20) pumping a tower she had just built, with 5-10 knights touching. 917851391 lost 5 per turn over t36-t43 (38 HP); 917986038 lost 3-4 per turn over t29-t35 (19 HP). Across the 13 won races she stood under contact on at most 2 turns per game (at most 4 HP), and top-ups under contact cost 9 HP in total.

At the same crowd size, standing costs about twice as much as moving. In the batch, turns with a knight touching cost 1.36 HP when she moved (97 turns) and 3.07 when she stood (29 turns). With 4-5 knights within 250 the costs were 1.6-1.9 moving vs 3.0-3.3 standing, and standing with 6 or more cost 4.6. A kiting queen is touched only by the lead knight: 917847874 t30-t35 (5 knights) and 917987888 t36-t42 (4 knights) lost exactly 1 per turn, while 917847874's single standing turn (t29) cost 3. Simultaneous hits on a standing queen topped out at 5 (917851391, 10 knights), presumably because the site she touches blocks part of her perimeter.

The standing is play()'s fallback, not a choice. Once the defence rule is satisfied, a BUILD on the touched own tower under threat happens only when kite() returns no step. kite() presumably finds no heading that gains 5 when she is surrounded, and with KITE=2 it may only end steps inside tower range (in 917986038 t29-t32 only the fresh tower 14, range 257-397, covered her). The bot then tops up the touched tower below 700 HP and, past 700, the flee rule BUILDs the nearest own tower, which is the same one. So she pumps it to 796 HP while being hit (917851391 t37-t43).

The big crowds come from merged releases: a second group enters 500 while the first is still on her. 917851391 had three merges (within 500: 3->7 at t31, 6->10 at t35, 5->9 at t45), with 12 knights spawned in the window by a forward opponent, about 19.5 HP each at the peak. 917986038 merged 5->7 at t27. 3 of 4 lost races had a merge against 1 of 13 won races (917851042, t48, late). Won races peaked at 5 or fewer knights within 250; the disasters peaked at 10 and 7. With 10 knights inside two towers (4-8 damage per turn) no knight died for 10 turns (917851391 t32-t42): aging (1 HP per knight per turn) killed faster than our towers.

The defence rule (fewer than 2 own towers within 500 and a knight within 250: build on the nearest free site) fired mid-wave when the queen hovered around 500 from her second tower after kiting or expanding. In 917851391 at t32 (tower 4 at 515) it caused a 4-turn walk west into the knights to site 18 (-1, -2, -4, -4). In 917986038 at t28, t33 and t38 (tower 17 at 528, 504, 550) it flapped between walking to site 5 and pumping 14. The same walks to new sites with 3 or fewer knights cost about 1 HP per turn in won races (917848456, 917849110, 917988974).

Zero- and one-HP won races (917847017, 917848088, 917850373, 917984480) had 2-3 towers at contact, at least one with 700+ HP within about 200 of the queen. The knights died at 113-270 and reached her only once (917984480 t41, -1). Their top-ups were safe because they happened only while no knight touched her: she alternated top-up and kite step.

Contact away from strong towers makes contact last longer even without standing. 917986038 met the wave at 483 from tower 17, whose range was 490; her tower potential on hit turns was 3.9 per knight, against 5.0-7.8 in every other game. 917987888 (a 68/68 HP tie, counted as won only through the seat-0 rule) walked away from strong tower 1 to build fresh towers 14 and 13. On 11 of its 17 hit turns no 500+ HP tower covered her, and the contact cost 21 HP at about 1 HP per turn.

Being caught walking to, or standing on, a new ladder site at the contact turn is common to both outcomes (10 of 17 games: 3 of 4 lost, 7 of 13 won) and does not separate them by itself. What separates them is what follows when the crowd grows: standing, or walking into the knights.

Two of the four losses (917847322: 9 HP; 917982302: 2 HP) had ordinary first waves with no standing under contact; their deficits (17 and 13) built up later. In this batch the first wave decided 2 of 4 losses and nearly cost one win (917987888, 68/68).

patterns: The first wave decided 8 of the 9 lost races. In each, its 20-turn cost was at least the final HP gap: 917982822 4 vs -1, 917849572 9 vs -9, 917845741 7 vs -7, 917988770 11 vs -7, 917848042 31 vs -24, 917985912 11 vs -5, 917982305 5 vs -1, 917985551 16 vs -3. Only 917846063 (0 vs -29) was lost later. Halving the first-wave cost would flip several races.

Kiting slows the knights but does not stop them. While she kites with a gap, they close about 25 per turn (batch 22.5 lost / 27.3 won; all races 27.9 / 24.7). Once a knight reaches her (nearest about 50 at each turn start), it stays on her until the towers or ageing kill it, costing 1-2 HP per turn. Turns with a knight within 60: lost 6.0 per game vs won 3.25 in the batch (all races 5.75 vs 3.03).

The defence rule is the most common way she gets caught. When fewer than 2 own towers stand within 500 and a knight is within 250, she walks to the nearest free site and builds there. The first hit came during that walk or the build in 4 of 9 lost games (917849572 t21, 917988770 t23-24, 917848042 t25-26, 917982822 t21) and in 2 of 8 won games (917847372 t24-26, 917848182 t26-29). Each such wave cost 4-31 HP. Afterwards she kites around the new tower (196 HP, range about 260, 3 damage per shot), because KITE_PULL pulls her toward the nearest own tower whatever its HP. In the batch this is a cost both groups pay, not a separator: the two won cases lost 18 and 14 HP.

Standing still with knights near her roughly doubles the loss. When kite() finds no step that gains 5, the touch rule tops up the tower she touches and she stands. Won games had the same in 917848540 (t38/40/44/45 -2 x4) and 917851508 t37 -2. Top-ups with a knight within 150: lost 11 turns / 22 HP over 9 games vs won 5 / 10 over 8. Over all traces, with a knight within 60 at the turn start, a standing turn costs 1.5-1.7 times a moving one at the same number of knights within 250: 2 knights 1.80 vs 1.22, 3 knights 1.93 vs 1.38, 4 knights 2.57 vs 1.53, 5 knights 3.08 vs 1.96, 6+ knights 4.55 vs 2.77.

Lost waves were stronger against fewer towers. Knight HP at contact was 60.4 vs 50.4 (16.2 vs 14.2 per knight). Towers covering the queen at contact: 1.33 vs 2.00. Tower damage per knight-turn within 500: 1.75 vs 2.62. The queen's distance to her nearest tower at contact: 160 vs 113, with 4 lost games at 169-289 because she was out on the build order.

Second groups and continuous streams joined before the first group was cleared: 917848042 (4 knights about every 9 turns, never cleared), 917985551 (every 5 turns), and 917845741, 917985912, 917988770 (a second batch 9-10 turns later). Among won games: 917848540 (merged to 8) and 917847372.

Edge kiting lets the knights catch up. She shuttles or runs into a wall: 917845741 t25-28 (y 58-78, the new tower against the top wall), 917983678 t37-40 (x 262->64), 917847372 t29-35 (y 58-102), and 917985551 t85-86 (y 45-63, after the window).

All four zero-loss waves (917846063, 917850788, 917988636, 917849341) had 2 or more towers at contact. She started kiting at contact (nearest 171-248), often circling a strong tower's site 90-105 from its centre, and the towers killed the knights before they reached her. Circling a site was not a reliable shield, though: circling that started after the knights reached her (917988770, 917849572, 917848042) did not shake them.

Caveat on the batch: towers at contact split it (1 tower: 6 of 9 lost vs 2 of 8 won), but the all-race split from summary.csv says this is not the main gap. With 1 tower at contact, won and lost races both pay about 10-12 HP (won 10.0, lost 11.7; 28 won, 27 lost). With 2 towers, won races lose 2.6 and lost races 18.2 (26 vs 12). This batch has only two 2-tower lost races (917982305: 5, 917846063: 0), so the large 2-tower losses must be in other readers' batches.

All-race breakdown of the 6.65-HP gap, using turns where a knight is within 60 at the turn start: top-ups 3.16 vs 0.52 HP per game (+2.64), kiting 4.66 vs 2.63 (+2.03), building a new tower 1.34 vs 0.63 (+0.71), walking to a new site 1.16 vs 0.63 (+0.53), turns without a knight that close +0.62. During those top-ups she has 5.1 knights within 250 in lost races vs 3.7 in won races.

H6 is not refuted on direction, but only part of it holds up. The "forward with fresher knights" part survives; the "far from her towers" and "walking the ladder" parts do not.

1. **Forward contacts carry the gap, and only in lost races.** In won races a forward contact costs nothing extra (5.7 HP vs 6.0 when not forward). Within forward contacts, lost races meet:
   - fresher knights: hpPerK0 15.9 vs 13.6, p=0.007;
   - more wave HP: 60.6 vs 49.6, p=0.008, at the same knight count (3.8 vs 3.6);
   - quicker follow-up knights: maximum knight HP within 500 over the first 5 turns 79.8 vs 55.1 (p=0.0006); maximum knights within 500 over 10 turns 5.5 vs 4.3 (p=0.006).
   
   Within forward contacts, these do not differ: nearTower0 (178 vs 164, p=0.39), towers, cover, contact turn, ladderWalk (52 % vs 42 %, p=0.59). Tower fire on the knights before contact is only slightly lower (9.1 vs 11.8, p=0.09). The forward-contact losses therefore look like fresher and sooner follow-up groups (the H7 idea), not like distance from her towers.

2. **"Forward" here is direction, not distance.** Distance from her start is the same (376 vs 367, p=0.88). She is further along x (+64) but further back along y (-53); the two correlate at rho -0.65. She is nearer the enemy start by 48 [5, 93] and nearer the centre by 56.

3. **Her towers are not further forward in lost races.** I located the tower centres from the queen's positions and the listed distances (residual RMS < 0.4). The most-forward tower sits at 435 vs 430 (p=0.9) and the strongest at 364 vs 369. She stands ahead of her towers in lost races (+9 vs -50, p=0.034), but only in the contact >24 and towers 2+ strata.

4. **Confound checks:**
   - The hpPerK0 difference is fully explained by forward0: the lost coefficient falls to t=0.61 once forward0 is controlled.
   - forward0 correlates with wave HP (rho 0.48). With startHp and wave HP controlled, forward0 no longer predicts lossK20 (-0.005 ± 0.008), which fits forward acting through fresher waves. nearTower0 still predicts it (+0.026 ± 0.010).
   - Within won races forward0 does not predict lossK20 (rho -0.01); within lost races it does (+0.31).
   - startHp is unrelated to the measures (|rho| <= 0.05), and the effects are similar in both startHp halves.
   - Seat: the forward0 difference appears only in seat 1 (+98, p=0.002) and not in seat 0 (+41, p=0.65).
   - Opponents met with both outcomes (11): lost > won on forward0 for 8 of them and on hpPerK0 for 9.
   - Dropping contacts after turn 40: forward0 +43 [+2, +86] p=0.046; durIdx0 +1.14, p=0.005.

5. **What this means for the rule lever.** "Stay within about 120 of a strong tower" targets a channel that carries at most 4-33 % of the gap, and she already spends the same time away from strong towers in won and lost races. "Keep the ladder's walks near home" targets the forward contact, which holds the whole gap but is harmless in won races. A useful trigger would need to react to the wave's freshness or the follow-up groups, i.e. be combined with H7.

ANSWER
- The size of the enemy's knight pressure decides the first wave. What matters is whether a second release joins the first while it is still on our queen (a merged wave or a stream). Our preparation does not decide it, and neither does how the queen handles a crowd of a given size.
- The bot has one rule that amplifies a bigger crowd. When kite() finds no covered step that gains 5, she stands and pumps a tower with knights in reach, usually the tower just built during the wave. That costs about 1.6-2.3 times a moving turn with the same knights.
- Why the crowd matters:
  - Each knight in contact costs 1 HP a turn, and knights are faster (100 against 60).
  - A tower shoots one knight for 3-5 HP a turn, and each knight loses 1 HP a turn to age.
  - Our towers' damage is the same in both groups: 84 against 89 per 20 turns.
  - So a larger or fresher crowd stays on her longer and closer. Lost races have 12.95 turns with a knight within 250 against 10.71, at 0.97 HP each against 0.55.
- Where the gap sits:
  - Contact after turn 24: 14.77 against 3.46 HP. With 2 or more towers at contact: 13.76 against 2.50.
  - With contact at turn 24 or earlier the gap is 10.27 against 9.00, and with one tower 11.74 against 9.96; neither is significant.

HOW THE 6.65 HP SPLITS (my own pass over the same traces; lossK20 matches summary.csv in 106 of 106)
- By command (no overlaps), lost minus won:
  - BUILD on an own tower, almost all standing (top-up or the flee BUILD): +2.81
  - Kite MOVE: +2.38, plus +0.14 for MOVEs that were blocked
  - BUILD on a free site, standing (building, or pinned): +0.86
  - BUILD on a free site, walking: +0.49
- By crowd: turns with 5 or more knights within 250 hold +3.97 (60 %).
- By turn type. Lines are grouped by knights within 250 × standing or moving × nearest knight within 155; the split is averaged over both groups' rates.
  - Lost races have more crowded turns: 3.7 HP (56 %, CI 1.3-8.4).
  - At the same crowd and stance, knights are already within 155 more often: 2.5 HP (38 %).
  - She stands more at the same crowd: 0.4 HP (5 %, CI -0.3 to 0.9).
  - The cost per turn differs at the same crowd, stance and reach: 0.1 HP.
  - So the physics and her stand rate are the same in both groups. Exposure is what differs.

RANKED MECHANISMS (share of the 6.65 HP gap)
1. Merged or streamed enemy releases, which make a bigger, fresher crowd (H7, with the freshness part of H6). Supported, and driven by the opponent.
   - The wave merged in 19 of 44 lost races against 7 of 62 won. The odds ratio is about 7 in every stratum.
   - 16 of the 19 lost merges follow an enemy spawn within the previous 7 turns. The merge comes at a median of 3 turns after contact, before most of the loss.
   - Loss after the merge accounts for the whole gap. Controlling for peak knight HP within 500, the lost coefficient falls from 6.65 to 1.65 (about 75 % explained).
   - A merged wave costs no more than an unmerged wave of the same peak size (coefficient -2.1, not significant).
   - Kiting cannot open distance against a stream. With one knight within 250, a kite move gains +50 in lost races against +112 in won.
   - No bot rule creates the merge; our rules only decide how the crowd is met (below).
2. Standing within reach at an own tower when kite() returns null (H1). Supported, an amplifier of mechanism 1.
   - Accounts for +2.81 HP (42 %): 1.25 such turns per lost race against 0.32. They occur in 17 of 44 lost races against 11 of 62 won.
   - 88 % of that HP is the touch-rule top-up of a tower below 700 HP. Of the 3.61 HP, 2.77 is at towers built during the wave, and 2.20 is on turns with 5 or more knights.
   - Per turn, standing costs more than moving at the same crowd and distance. In contact: 2.92 against 1.27 HP with 4 knights within 250, and 4.38 against 2.30 with 6 or more.
   - If these turns cost a kite MOVE, about 1.0-1.4 HP of the gap is recoverable (15-20 %). That is my 1.30 HP (CI 0.30-2.47), or H1's 0.97-1.17. Lost races would save 1.8 HP and won races 0.5. All else equal, 2 of 44 lost races would flip.
   - Code in MainBot.java (line numbers):
     - kite(), 236-270, returns null unless a step beats the current score + 5 (line 252). The score is the nearest-knight distance minus 100 % (KITE_PULL) of the distance to the nearest own tower (line 265). Each step must end covered (line 260), and the prediction ignores units (Physics.queenStep).
     - Then the touch rule tops up an own tower below TOWER_HP 700 (lines 116-117), or the flee rule BUILDs the nearest own tower (lines 128-131).
3. A kite step re-fires the defence rule at the 500 edge, followed by pumping the new tower (H4). Weak on average, decisive in the tail.
   - It happens equally often: in 6 of 44 lost races and 6 of 62 won. The adjusted share is 0.3-1.1 HP (5-17 %); the raw upper bound is 1.86.
   - The 3 costliest lost races, 917851391, 917982299 and 917986038, are this chain. A kite step carries her 500-550 from her second tower. The defence rule then walks her 1-6 turns into the knights, and the touch rule pumps the new 196-HP tower at 4-6 HP a turn. These 3 races alone hold 2.6 HP of the gap (39 %).
   - Example, 917982299: two towers at contact and 1 HP in 4 kite turns. Then 12 HP on the walk to site 4, 27 HP building and pumping it with 6 knights on her, and 17 HP kiting afterwards. Lost by 14.
   - Code: the defence rule (lines 95-105) counts own towers within THREAT_RADIUS 500, and kite() never checks that count.
4. A BUILD that cannot land while she barely moves (H2). Weak, and it overlaps mechanisms 2 and 3.
   - The HP lost on those turns differs by 1.51, but a pinned turn costs no more than a standing BUILD that lands (-0.09 HP per race). The lever is at most 0.87 HP and probably about 0.3 per lost race; 2 races hold 37 of the 79 HP.
   - Code: the defence BUILD (line 103) and the flee BUILD (line 130) walk in a straight line, not through walkTo or the route planner. Nothing remembers that the last one did not move her.
   - In 917850428 one of our own knights wedged her for about 20 turns, so the planner, which ignores units, would not have helped either.
5. Kiting covered by one tower (H5). Weak.
   - It accounts for 0.86 HP (13 %), and the result is fragile. Being bound to one tower costs about 0 HP per turn.
   - The tower that does not reach her is the fresh one, about 70 beyond its range. The cause is that the kite score (line 265) pulls only toward the nearest tower.
6. A forward contact as a location (H6). Not a separate mechanism.
   - The whole gap sits in forward contacts: 15.8 against 5.7 HP. But in won races a forward contact costs nothing extra.
   - The effect disappears once wave HP is controlled, so it is the freshness part of mechanism 1.
- Refuted:
  - H3, the defence walk and build: +1.36 HP, CI -0.19 to 3.10, Hodges-Lehmann shift 0, equal cost per turn in both groups.
  - H8, knights held off by a site: about 0.2 HP.
  - H9, kiting against the board edge: about 0.27 HP.
- Pricing every BUILD turn with a knight in reach (mechanisms 2-4 together) at the kite rate closes at most about 1.9 HP (29 %, CI 0.45-3.76), with about 5 naive flips.

PROPOSED RULE CHANGES (in order of expected value)
- R1: never stand with a knight in reach (from H1). New parameter STAND_REACH=155: contact 55 plus knight speed 100. H1 checked this cut-off: no standing turn with the nearest knight at 150 or more lost HP (0 of 545).
  - In kite(), when an enemy knight is within STAND_REACH, start bestScore at minus infinity instead of the current score + 5.
  - Keep the existing limits: the step must move at least MIN_STEP, end covered by an own tower and stay out of enemy tower range.
  - The top-up and the flee BUILD then fire only when no covered step moves her. The defence rule keeps its priority.
  - Optional arm: apply it only with 3 or more knights within 250 (recovers 1.18 HP of the gap) or 5 or more (0.98 HP).
- R2: keep the second tower within the radius while kiting (from H4). In kite(), if THREAT_TOWERS_NEAR own towers are within THREAT_RADIUS now, drop steps that end with fewer. An alternative is hysteresis: count towers out to about 560 while the threat lasts.
  - In Gold this would act in about 11 % of races.
  - Pair it with R1, because more moves mean more edge crossings.
- R3: react to a failed BUILD (from H2). If last turn's BUILD toward the same untouched site moved her less than 10 and a knight is within 155, take R1's forced step. For the defence rule, the next free site is the alternative.
- R4 (lowest priority, from H5): in the kite score, add C per extra covering tower at the step's end, with C 25 or 50. Expected gain 0-0.9 HP.

WHAT THE DATA DOES NOT SUPPORT
- That lost races are worse prepared or played worse:
  - Same contact turn (27.9/28.1), towers (1.64/1.73), knights within 500 (3.70/3.47), top-ups, kiting moves and distance to the tower.
  - Same stand rate and cost per turn at equal crowd.
  - WAVE_TOWERS=2 and TOPUP_FROM=2 already lost locally, with S about 0.45.
- That the queen causes the merge (16 of 19 lost merges follow an enemy spawn), or that a merge costs more than an unmerged wave of the same peak size.
- The defence walk (H3), site shields (H8) or the board edge (H9) as causes. H5's premise that she is bound to a fresh tower is backwards: the one tower covering her is the old strong one.
- A large gain in results:
  - Even if lost races' first wave cost the won-race mean, at most 12 of 44 lost races would flip naively.
  - R1 flips about 2, and R1-R3 at most about 5.
  - Merged waves predict losing even at equal first-wave loss.
  - Lost races also lose 6.5 HP against the enemy's 2.8 on turns 200-250.
- Things the traces do not measure: the value of the top-ups forgone for later waves, whether moving breaks up the crowd later, queen deaths (25 of the 69 losses are excluded), and anything after contact + 29.
- The effects depend on a few races: the medians of the stand, pinned, re-trigger and single-cover measures (H1, H2, H4, H5) are all 0. Without the 3 costliest lost races, H1's difference is 1.32 HP (CI 0.05-2.70).

**Verdict:** the size of the gap and the extra cost of standing per turn hold up. The three mechanisms blame the wrong cause: in the races we lost, the wave caught the queen further forward, and she often moved further forward during it. My parser matches lossK20 in all 106 races, and the synthesis's synth.py gives identical output when rerun. No repository file was changed and Gradle and Java were not run.

**Main finding the synthesis misses: position at contact.** fx is the queen's distance from her own back edge.
- Lost races meet the first wave further forward: 444 vs 380 (difference 64, CI 14..116). In the stratum where the gap sits (contact after turn 24 and 2+ towers), it is 500 vs 381 (CI 25..216).
- Split at the median fx at contact (407):
  - Forward half: lost 15.79 vs won 5.62 HP (difference 10.2, CI 4.1..16.5).
  - Back half: 6.20 vs 6.03 (no gap). The split holds for cut-offs from 350 to 450.
  - Lost races: 29 of 53 forward against 15 of 53 back (p 0.010). Merged waves: 20 of 53 against 6 of 53 (p 0.003).
- Forwardness goes with later contact (r 0.41) and with more forward own towers (mean fx 426 vs 312). It looks like base layout plus the ladder, not the opponent.

**Claim 1 (merged or streamed enemy releases, driven by the opponent): the link to losing holds; "driven by the opponent" is overstated; the "stream" sub-claim is wrong.**
- Holds:
  - Merged waves: 19 of 44 lost races against 7 of 62 won (odds ratio 6.0, p 0.0002).
  - Loss after the merge is the whole gap: 7.23 vs 0.58 HP per race. Unmerged races only: 6.68 vs 5.73 (CI −2.0..4.3).
  - Controlling for peak knight HP within 500, the lost coefficient falls from 6.65 to 1.65. A merged wave costs no more at the same peak (coefficient −2.10, SE 2.03).
  - Merges do follow a recent enemy spawn: 15 of 19 (not 16) within 7 turns, but 47% of other threatened turns also do (p 0.005).
- Overstated:
  - **"Odds ratio about 7 in every stratum":** it is 8.6 in the forward half and 1.4 in the back half, where there are only 6 merges.
  - **"No bot rule creates the merge":** on the merge turn the queen moved toward the enemy in 10 of 19 lost merges, against 27% of other threatened turns (p 0.016). That includes 8 of 11 kite-step merges, against 32% of kite steps (p 0.007).
  - A forward kite step is followed by 2 or more new knights within 500 in 9 of 108 cases (8.3%), against 5 of 243 (2.1%) for other kite steps.
  - The two costliest merges came during a defence walk of about 250 toward the enemy.
  - Enemy spawns in the window are not higher in lost races: 4.05 vs 4.48. The 19 lost merges are spread over 17 opponents.
  - **Peak HP is not an opponent-only measure:** it rises 9.6 HP per 100 fx (SE 1.9). The lost-minus-won gap in knight HP within 500 grows from 7.8 at contact to 19.3 at contact + 6. Controlling for it also removes our own positioning.
- Wrong: **"Kiting cannot open distance against a stream" (+50 vs +112 with one knight within 250).** Take only lines with no kill and no change in the knight count within 500. Then the gains are −37 vs −25 (difference −11, CI −25..0). The +50 vs +112 comes from turns where a knight died and the nearest distance jumped to the next knight (+130 vs +204).
- Within merged races, lost ones lose 20.2 HP against 7.0 for won ones (CI 6.3..21.1). Lost merged races are more forward (486 vs 407), have fewer towers (1.53 vs 2.00), more standing loss (7.2 vs 2.0) and 4 chains against 0. Only 7 won races merged, so this comparison is weak.

**Claim 2 (standing within reach at an own tower when kite() returns null): holds per turn; its size is overstated and fragile.**
- Holds:
  - HP: 3.61 vs 0.81 (difference 2.81, CI 0.85..5.08); 1.25 vs 0.32 lines per race; 17 of 44 lost races against 11 of 62 won.
  - Of the 3.61: 3.16 is top-up, 2.77 is at towers not standing at contact, and 2.20 is on turns with 5 or more knights.
  - Same game, within 6 turns, same knight count and distance band: standing costs 2.62 HP per line against 1.25 for a kite move. That holds in 18 of 19 games.
  - Move then stand at an equal crowd (3.75 to 3.83 knights): 1.25 rises to 2.21 HP.
  - Cut-off: 0 of 385 window standing lines (0 of 721 in all) at 150 or more lost HP. At 95-125, standing lines all lost HP (13 of 13, 1.69 each) against 14 of 104 moving lines (0.13).
- Overstated:
  - The top 3 lost races hold 45% of this HP (top 5, 64%). Without the top 3, the difference is 1.32 (CI 0.04..2.75).
  - Standing does not predict losing once crowd size is controlled: the logit coefficient goes from 1.07 (SE 0.45) to −0.00 (SE 0.63).
  - Lost-race stands are forward (fx 566 vs 386). At least 1.48 HP per race is pumping a tower the defence rule built in the same episode.
  - The 1.0-1.4 HP saving assumes a forced step costs what a chosen step costs, and that the forgone top-ups are worth nothing. In 917982299, pumping from 196 to 580 HP made the later kiting possible.
  - The trigger also fires in 11 of 62 won races. Example: 917846333, won by 5 with 16 HP of standing loss.

**Claim 3 (a kite step re-fires the defence rule at the 500 edge, then the new tower is pumped): overstated and partly misattributed.**
- Holds: chains occur in 6 of 44 lost races and 6 of 62 won. The kite steps move the second tower from 441-497 away to 500-550.
- Wrong: **"the 3 costliest lost races are this chain".**
  - 917986038 is 5th (29 HP). 917848042 (31, no chain) and 917987370 (31, chain episode 2 HP) cost more.
  - Its chain episodes cost 3 HP. About 18-22 HP is pumping tower 14 (built at contact, 188 to 572 HP) with 5-7 knights touching her, which is mechanism 2.
  - One of its re-fires came from knights pushing her during a top-up, not from a kite step.
- The chain's cost sits in two races, 917851391 and 917982299: 88 of 106 chain-episode HP. Both defence walks went about 250 toward the enemy (fx +248, +250).
- Won-race chains walked home in 5 of 6 (fx −11 to −72), costing 0-4 HP per episode.
- HP in the 10 turns after the first chain: 22.8 lost vs 7.0 won. But 917846826 crossed the 500 line 4 times, lost 18 HP and still won by 14.
- Defence episodes (walk, build and pump of a new site) carry 2.80 HP of the gap (CI 0.19..6.09). All of it is in forward episodes: 2.74 (CI 0.23..6.03), against 0.06 for the rest.

**The "where the gap sits" figures** match exactly (14.77/3.46, 13.76/2.50, 10.27/9.00, 11.74/9.96). The gap is fragile: without the 2, 3 or 5 costliest lost races it is 4.51, 4.01 or 2.98.

| Rule | Verdict | Reason |

| R1 (never stand with a knight in reach) | Holds, with smaller scope | Best-supported lever: about 1.3 HP of the gap, about 2 naive flips, fragile. Also fires in 11 of 62 won races. |

Better candidates: hysteresis on the 500 radius, and a defence rule that skips free sites lying toward the enemy or the knights. |
